level.title: Elementary: city, travel, routines, health
goals: Find your way around an Italian city
Talk about past trips with passato prossimo
Describe routines, health, and future plans

lessons.title: Around the city (a Roma, in Italia)
lessons.learn: Cities take A, countries take IN: VADO A ROMA (I go to Rome), VADO IN ITALIA (I go to Italy). Location uses STARE: STO A CASA (I am at home). Sinistra (left), destra (right), sempre dritto (straight)!

grammar.title: A + city · IN + country
grammar.explain: VADO A ROMA (city), VADO IN ITALIA (country). STO A CASA (at home). Big places take IN, dots on the map take A!
grammar.pattern: a + city · in + country · sto/stai/sta + place
mistakes: Saying VADO IN ROMA — cities take A: A ROMA.
Saying VADO A ITALIA — countries take IN: IN ITALIA.

lessons.title: Travel and passato prossimo
lessons.learn: Past trips: HO VISITATO (I visited). Passato prossimo = AVERE (ho, hai, ha) + past verb (visitATO, mangiATO, vedUTO). -ARE verbs just add ATO!

grammar.title: Passato prossimo: ho visitato
grammar.explain: HO + visitATO = I visited. HAI + mangiATO = you ate. HA + vedUTO = he/she saw. Most past verbs end ATO (from -ARE), UTO (-ERE), ITO (-IRE).
mistakes: Saying HO VIAGGIARE — past needs VIAGGIATO, not the infinitive.
Forgetting movement verbs use ESSERE: È ARRIVATA (she arrived).

dialogue.t: Sì, ho viaggiato in Messico. Ho visitato la spiaggia.
dialogue.r: see, oh vyahd-JAH-toh een MEHS-see-koh. oh vee-zee-TAH-toh lah SPYAHD-jah.
dialogue.en: Yes, I travelled in Mexico. I visited the beach.

lessons.title: Daily routines (reflexive verbs)
lessons.learn: Routines bounce back: MI ALZO = I get (myself) up. MI = myself, TI = yourself, SI = himself/herself. Mornings run on MI/TI/SI: alzarsi, lavarsi, vestirsi!

grammar.title: Reflexive MI/TI/SI: mi alzo
grammar.explain: ALZARSI = to get up. MI ALZO, TI ALZI, SI ALZA. The little word points back at the person — never drop it!

examples.en: Do you wash in the morning?

mistakes: Saying ALZO without MI — it means 'I lift', not 'I get up'!
Mixing TI and SI: TI = you, SI = he/she.

dialogue.en: What time do you get up?

dialogue.t: Mi alzo alle sette e faccio la doccia.
dialogue.r: mee AHLT-soh AHL-leh SEHT-teh eh FAHT-choh lah DOHT-chah.
dialogue.en: I get up at seven and shower.

lessons.title: Health and future plans
lessons.learn: At the doctor: MI FA MALE LA TESTA = my head hurts. For plans, Italians use the PRESENT + time word: PARTO DOMANI = I leave tomorrow (I am leaving tomorrow). Simple and natural!

grammar.title: Near future: present + time word
grammar.explain: PARTO DOMANI = I leave tomorrow. STUDI STASERA? = Are you studying tonight? Present tense + domani/stasera/lunedì = instant future. (Real futuro comes at B1!)
mistakes: Skipping the time word: PARTO alone = I leave (now?).
Using future endings too early — present + domani first!

lessons.title: Clothes and shopping (questo/quello)
lessons.learn: Shop in Italian! LA CAMICIA, LE SCARPE. Point with QUESTO (this, near me) and QUELLO (that, over there): QUESTA CAMICIA (this shirt), QUEL NEGOZIO (that shop).

grammar.title: QUESTO vs QUELLO: this vs that
grammar.explain: QUESTO/QUESTA = this (near me). QUELLO/QUELLA = that (far). QUELLO shortens like articles: QUEL vestito, QUELLA borsa, QUEI pantaloni, QUELLE scarpe.
mistakes: Saying QUESTO camicia — feminine: QUESTA camicia.
Saying QUELLO vestito — shorten it: QUEL vestito.

lessons.title: Weather scenes (faceva, c'era)
lessons.learn: Weather stories use IMPERFETTO: FACEVA BELLO (it was nice), C'ERA VENTO (there was wind). Just two phrases paint any past sky!

grammar.title: First imperfetto: faceva, c'era
grammar.explain: FACEVA BELLO/FREDDO/CALDO = it was nice/cold/hot. C'ERA + noun = there was…: C'ERA IL SOLE (there was sun). Weather past = imperfetto, always!
mistakes: Saying HA FATTO BELLO for scenes — weather stories use FACEVA.
Saying C'È for past — past needs C'ERA.

dialogue.en: It was nice. There was sun.
